semantics.note: The revision keeps the qualifier 'we see no reason to think', plus 'at all' and 'literally'. The first part reports the authors' reading of the evidence. The second describes the training objective and works as framing.

contract.note: The speaker gives no definition of 'stable representations' and no standard of evidence. Any verdict would need a standard the speaker did not supply, so treating the claim as not scorable is fair.

reviews.rationale: The claim is a qualified epistemic stance ('we see no reason to think') joined to a framing description of next-word prediction. 'Stable representations' is undefined, and no criterion separates limited state encoding from what the authors meant. Candidate probing studies were considered but cannot settle the claim without an added standard. Not adjudicable.

semantics.note: The proposition is a firm observation and keeps the 'at least not... reliable use' qualifier. 'Of the world' accurately glosses 'such cognitive models' as the context defines them.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: models that keep and update representations of entities, used repeatably, as shown in work up to the publication date. The reading is not stretched either way. Borderline demonstrations still depend on that reading.

evidence.note: Li, Nye and Andreas (2021), from before the post, find that natural-language models encode simple, editable states. However, the full state is recovered only 53.8% of the time, and the authors say the link to behaviour is only general. This does not show reliable use, and it is not a comprehensive assessment.
Accurate state tracking in transformers trained on chess notation, published before the post. The domain is chess notation, not natural language, so it falls outside the claim's scope.

reviews.rationale: No item in the packet shows a natural-language LLM reliably using its own updating world representations by 2022-06-22. e1 is limited and unreliable, and e2 covers chess, not natural language. The packet also lacks a comprehensive contemporary assessment that would meet the support condition, and the search does not rule out an earlier qualifying demonstration. Unresolved.
